chapter.li: Verse31 Then he took the twelve and said unto them, Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things which are written by the prophets concerning the Son of Man shall be accomplished, VerseEnd Verse32 for he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully treated, and spit on; VerseEnd Verse33 and they shall scourge and put him to death, and the third day he shall rise again. VerseEnd Verse34 And they understood none of these things, and this saying was hidden from them, neither remembered they the things which were spoken. VerseEnd

Verse35 And it came to pass, as he came near Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the wayside begging. VerseEnd Verse36 And hearing the multitude pass by, he asked what it meant. VerseEnd Verse37 And they told him that Jesus of Nazareth passed by. VerseEnd Verse38 And he cried, saying, Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me! VerseEnd Verse39 And they who went before rebuked him, telling him that he should hold his peace. But he cried so much the more, saying, Son of David, have mercy on me! VerseEnd Verse40 And Jesus stood and commanded him to be brought unto him. And when he had come near, he asked him, VerseEnd Verse41 saying, What do you desire that I shall do unto you? And he said, Lord, that I may receive my sight. VerseEnd Verse42 And Jesus said unto him, Receive your sight; your faith has saved you. VerseEnd Verse43 And immediately he received his sight and he followed him, glorifying God. And all the disciples, when they saw this, gave praise unto God. VerseEnd

LEChapter19 Verse1 And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho. VerseEnd Verse2 And behold, there was a man named Zacchaeus who was chief among the publicans, and he was rich. VerseEnd Verse3 And he sought to see Jesus, who he was, and could not for the crowd because he was little of stature. VerseEnd Verse4 And he ran before and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was to pass that way. VerseEnd Verse5 And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up and saw him, and said unto him, Zacchaeus, make haste and come down, for today I must abide at your house. VerseEnd Verse6 And he made haste and came down and received him joyfully. VerseEnd Verse7 And when the disciples saw it, they all murmured, saying that he had gone to be guest with a man who is a sinner. VerseEnd

Verse8 And Zacchaeus stood and said unto the Lord, Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor, and if I have taken anything from any man by unjust means, I restore fourfold. VerseEnd Verse9 And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forasmuch as he also is a son of Abraham, VerseEnd Verse10 for the Son of Man has come to seek and to save that which was lost. VerseEnd

Verse11 And as they heard these things, he added and spoke a parable because he was near to Jerusalem, and because the Jews taught that the kingdom of God should immediately appear. VerseEnd Verse12 He said therefore, A certain nobleman went into a far country to receive for himself a kingdom and to return. VerseEnd Verse13 And he called his ten servants, and he delivered them ten pounds and said unto them, Trade until I come. VerseEnd Verse14 But his citizens hated him and sent a messenger after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us. VerseEnd Verse15 And it came to pass that when he had returned, having received the kingdom, then he commanded these servants to be called unto him, to whom he had given the money, that he might know how much every man had gained by trading. VerseEnd

Verse16 Then came the first, saying, Lord, your pound has gained ten pounds. VerseEnd Verse17 And he said unto him, Well done you good servant; because you have been faithful in a very little, have authority over ten cities. VerseEnd Verse18 And the second came, saying, Lord, your pound has gained five pounds. VerseEnd Verse19 And he said likewise to him, Be also over five cities. VerseEnd Verse20 And another came, saying, Lord, behold your pound which I have kept laid up in a napkin, VerseEnd Verse21 for I feared you because you are an austere man: you take up that you laid not down, and reap that which you do not sow. VerseEnd Verse22 And he said unto him, Out of your own mouth will I judge you, O wicked servant. You knew that I was an austere man, taking up that which I laid not down, and reaping that I did not sow. VerseEnd Verse23 Why then did you not give my money into the bank, that at my coming I might have received my own with usury? VerseEnd Verse24 And he said unto them who stood by, Take from him the pound and give to him who has ten pounds. VerseEnd Verse26 For I say unto you that unto everyone who trades shall be given, and from him who trades not, even that he has received shall be taken away from him. VerseEnd Verse27 But those my enemies who desire not that I should reign over them, bring them here and slay them before me. VerseEnd
